title: Month-End Close: Route Incentive Review
description: The board wants to know whether the BudgetAir incentive created value or just lit cash on fire with a commemorative match.

questions.prompt: Why should the airport track route incentive expense separately?
choices: Because separating the incentive from normal operating expenses allows management to evaluate route contribution and avoid hiding subsidies inside generic cost buckets.
Because incentives should never be recorded in the ledger.
Because all route incentives automatically become passenger facility charge revenue.
Because separate tracking lets the airport ignore the cash effect.

questions.prompt: Passenger volume increased after the incentive. Why might the decision still be financially weak?
choices: Because volume growth only creates value if incremental revenue and contribution exceed incentive cost and added operating burden.
Because passenger growth is always bad for an airport.
Because higher traffic eliminates all operating costs.
Because incentives should be judged only by press coverage.

questions.prompt: Why can a debt-funded incentive create pressure even if cash increases from the Debt Desk?
choices: Because the borrowing improves liquidity now but adds interest expense and leverage risk in future periods.
Because new debt always counts as revenue.
Because interest expense disappears when passenger volume rises.
Because debt-funded cash never has to be repaid.

questions.prompt: What should the CFO present to the board?
choices: A bridge from incentive cost to incremental revenue, margin impact, cash effect, and risk - not just passenger growth.
Only the marketing headline from the carrier.
A cash balance with no explanation of debt or expense.
